tldr: For the exact balanced projection-Gibbs specialization of Chen--Yu's soft quadratic law, with Gaussian-generated cohorts frozen before assignment and \(d/n\in[1/8,3/8]\), we prove a computable variance map with \(\eta(k,\beta)=2/(1+\beta+\sqrt{(1+\beta)^2-4\beta k})\). A two-replica argument gives a uniform cohort tail bound \(O_{w_0,\epsilon}(n^{-1/8})\) for the conditional Kolmogorov error on every fixed positive variance floor. Observed arm regressions with an inverse-Gram trace correction yield a feasible conservative interval for realized SATE. Its scale attains the smallest uniformly conservative envelope among regular original-record DIM-centered limiting Wald scales, and its coverage is asymptotically exact precisely when \(\rho_n\to1\) along sequences with positive limiting variance. Explicit regression diagnostics, a finite envelope fallback, and a minimum radius make the procedure total. These asymptotic statements concern the proportional Gaussian-generated restriction, not every fixed population in Chen--Yu's carrier.
gap: Chen--Yu already contains the soft quadratic assignment law. Wang--Li excludes proportional dimension under its displayed approximation condition. The checked Gaussianized-design theorem has a different assignment law, and existing many-regressor inference uses a treatment-covariate independence input unavailable under full-array Gibbs balancing.
fill: A computable variance map, a normal approximation conditional on both frozen potential-outcome vectors, and an attainable observable Wald envelope connect prospectively specified balancing to feasible causal inference. The analytic reduction is derived rather than assumed.
